title: Keyturn Host Protection Plan Terms on Moving a Vehicle Between Plans
content:
A host may move a vehicle between plans of the Keyturn Host Protection Plan, and the move takes effect on a future date rather than the day it is asked for, so that cover on a trip already running is never changed underneath it.

### The notice and the effective day

The host must give the plan's notice, and the change then takes effect the plan's effective period after the notice is recorded, counted in whole calendar days from the day the notice is taken, with the day of notice itself not counted. The day the notice was recorded is read from the enrolment record for the enrolment being changed, and the effective day is reached when the plan's effective period in whole calendar days has passed; the change stands on that day and on every day after it, and not before.

### Direction of the move

Moving to a plan with a larger earnings share is a downgrade of cover, and after a downgrade the host may not downgrade again until the plan's lockout period has run; moving to a plan with a smaller earnings share is an upgrade and carries no lockout.

### While a claim is open

A plan change is refused outright while a claim on that enrolment is open, because the plan in force when the loss occurred is the plan that settles it, and changing plans midway would leave the claim under two sets of limits. Whether a claim stands open is read, before the change is made, from the claim records standing against that same enrolment.

### The target plan's own limits

The vehicle must satisfy the target plan's own age, odometer, value and title limits on the day the change takes effect, not merely on the day it is asked for. A restated declared value is treated as a plan change where the new value moves the vehicle outside the current plan's value band, and as an ordinary correction where it does not.

### Boundary illustration (hypothetical)

Where a plan publishes an effective period of 21 calendar days and notice is recorded on a given day, the day of notice is not counted: the change stands on the twenty-first day after it, and a move attempted on the twentieth day after notice has not yet reached its effective day.
